mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which can stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher than baseline during low FEDFUNDS periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts reflect strong consumer demand, signaling economic expansion and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase but SPX returns are negative over 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate indicates labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises 0.2pp but SPX returns are positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production suggests supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production declines but SPX returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts combined with low federal funds rate indicates strong demand and easy monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts and FEDFUNDS signal fails to correlate with positive SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment may not prevent economic downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Low UNRATE in late-cycle doesn't lead to negative SPX returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth indicates strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth doesn't correlate with positive SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Employment growth combined with rising retail sales indicates strong labor market and demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS and RSAFS signal fails to predict positive SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03).
